reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, the current five-set partition shows weak nominal correspondence with clinical grade (Cramer's V 0.185, p=0.045) and M stage (0.247, p=0.028), with the M-stage signal localized to K5_C0003 (set-versus-rest p=0.0145). No correspondence is detected for overall stage (p=0.244) or T stage (p=0.706). Against previously reported expression-derived taxonomies, agreement is low: ClearCode34 ARI 0.114 / AMI 0.149 (reference_n=76) and TCGA m1-m4 ARI 0.052 / AMI 0.045 (reference_n=84). These are correspondence observations only; the taxonomy comparisons overlap the RNA discovery view and are not independent validation, and none of these results establishes novelty, validity, independence, or retention of any candidate set.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The weak clinical-grade and M-stage correspondence is consistent with the partition-scope confounder report, which found partition-wide technical/acquisition associations (e.g., tissue source site Cramer's V 0.346, q=0.003), indicating that some partition structure tracks measured non-biological factors. The low taxonomy agreement is consistent with the biological-support reports, which describe distinct transcriptomic and mutation phenotypes per set that do not map cleanly onto established ccRCC taxonomies.
limitations: Known-label correspondence is not external validation; ClearCode34 and TCGA m1-m4 overlap the RNA discovery view.
Clinical grade and M-stage associations are weak and nominal; no multiplicity adjustment across the clinical-label family is reported.
M-stage has missing_n=5 (available_n=98); grade, stage, and T stage are complete (available_n=103).
Taxonomy reference coverage is partial (reference_n=76 for ClearCode34, 84 for TCGA m1-m4).
Correspondence or non-correspondence does not by itself establish novelty, validity, independence, or retention.
